en: When the President vetoes a bill, Congress can override it if two-thirds of both houses vote to pass it again, making it a law.
Fe del Mundo designed a bamboo incubator that uses warm water in outer containers to regulate inner temperatures, keeping premature babies warm without electricity.
Ifugao farmers build stone-walled rice terraces so gravity channels mountain spring water downward through stepped pools to irrigate the crops.
The carabao’s wide, splayed hooves distribute its heavy body weight, preventing the animal from sinking deeply into soft rice paddy mud.
Early Filipinos traded gold, beeswax, and tortoise shells with Chinese merchants because local artisans lacked kiln technology to produce porcelain.
Ramon Barba discovered that spraying potassium nitrate on mango trees triggers florigen production, forcing the trees to flower simultaneously for higher fruit yields.
Citizens register with COMELEC to receive a voter ID, which election officers scan to verify their identity before they cast ballots.
During the Sinulog festival, dancers step forward and backward to drum beats to mimic the flowing movement of the river current.
Ancient Filipinos carved Baybayin characters on bamboo using sharp knives, following the wood's grain to prevent splintering and ruining the text.
In bayanihan, neighbors lift a traditional nipa hut by pushing its bamboo poles upward, allowing the family to relocate the entire house.
When a local government unit collects real property taxes, the treasury allocates a specific percentage to fund public schools and health clinics.
Katipuneros tore their cedulas to physically destroy tax records, signaling their definitive break from Spanish colonial rule and starting the Philippine Revolution.
